answer: The hatter presses every brim with the iron and logs the heat and the fur it came from against the hat it shapes. A umber hat bought from a pedlar fails the log: at the yarrow of the iron the brim must match the hatter's own pressing, and a pedlar's hat loses its brim in the rain. Forging a hat means hiring a hatter, buying false fur and paying 7,300, and the velvet line in the brim-iron log is kept for seven years, so a hat whose brim was never pressed is crushed.
